lead.headline: SOUTH BENGALURU MAN ARRESTED IN MURDER OF LIVE-IN PARTNER'S 18-YEAR-OLD SON
lead.deck: Police arrested a 44-year-old man over the killing of an engineering student and an attack on the student's mother at a south Bengaluru home.
paragraphs: A 44-year-old man was arrested Friday over the alleged murder of his partner's 18-year-old son and an attack on the boy's mother at their rented home in south Bengaluru.
Police said the incident took place on November 16. The engineering student, Soham Das, died; his mother was injured and is receiving treatment. The investigation is ongoing.

sidebarStory.headline: POLICE SEARCH FOR MEDICAL STUDENT AFTER SHE IS DRAGGED INTO SUV ON CAMPUS
sidebarStory.subhead: The Mangaluru incident prompted a probe after video clips spread online.
paragraphs: Police in Mangaluru registered a case and began efforts to trace a medical student allegedly taken from Kanachur Medical College by relatives opposed to her interfaith relationship.
The Indian Express said it could not verify the circulating video. Police said the woman is an adult and has the right to decide where she lives and with whom.

groups.ariaLabel: Bengaluru and Karnataka civic, infrastructure and employment news

stories.headline: POLICE CAN PRESS CORRUPTION CHARGES AGAINST THREE KPSC OFFICERS
paragraphs: Karnataka has allowed police to invoke the Prevention of Corruption Act against suspended KPSC chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar, commission member B V Geetha and IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar.
The move could enable prosecution under the stricter law as investigators pursue alleged irregularities in a recruitment scam.

stories.headline: STATE ORDERS PROBE INTO VIRAL VIDEO OF TAMIL NADU MINISTER ON TIGER SAFARI
paragraphs: Karnataka has ordered an inquiry after a video appeared to show Tamil Nadu minister Vanni Arasu pursuing wildlife in a reserve using a forest department vehicle.
Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy said the rules apply regardless of a visitor's status. The video appeared to show a tiger and elephants; authorities are examining the circumstances.

stories.headline: FIR FILED OVER ALLEGED REMARKS ABOUT SOCIAL REFORMER BASAVANNA
paragraphs: Police registered a case against writer Ravi Hanj and publisher Vishweshwar Bhat over alleged derogatory remarks about 12th-century social reformer Basavanna in the book Basava Mantapa and a later interview.
The book has drawn objections from sections of the Veerashaiva-Lingayat community and criticism from leaders of both the Congress and BJP.

groups.ariaLabel: India court decisions, public safety and shipping news

stories.headline: NIKHIL GUPTA SENTENCED TO MORE THAN 19 YEARS IN US ASSASSINATION PLOT
paragraphs: Nikhil Gupta, 55, was sentenced in New York to just over 19½ years in prison for conspiring to hire a hit man to kill Sikh separatist leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, an American citizen.
Gupta apologised in court. The sentence follows his guilty plea in the murder-for-hire plot, according to prosecutors and court records reported by the Associated Press.

stories.headline: YOUTH CONGRESS PROTESTS META ACCOUNT RESTRICTIONS IN HYDERABAD
paragraphs: Telangana Youth Congress workers protested outside Meta's Hyderabad office after accounts belonging to two national office-bearers were restricted.
Workers alleged political interference and demanded that the accounts be restored. Police detained state party leaders and other protesters, NDTV reported.

stories.headline: SUPREME COURT QUASHES LAND ACQUISITION AFTER GRAM SABHA REJECTION
paragraphs: The Supreme Court set aside Odisha's acquisition of land in three Sundargarh villages for a Dalmia Cement mining project, finding that prior Gram Sabha consent had not been obtained.
The court noted that the two village assemblies had rejected the proposal in 2020, Bar and Bench reported.

groups.ariaLabel: India energy, technology and culture news

stories.headline: CYCLONE AKVAN WEAKENS INTO DEEP DEPRESSION OVER SOUTH ODISHA
paragraphs: The IMD said Cyclone Akvan weakened into a deep depression over coastal Odisha on Friday morning, near Gopalpur, after moving north-northeast across the coast.
The system was forecast to continue northward and weaken further. The bulletin lists the storm's position and movement as of 11:30 am IST on November 20.

stories.headline: DAWOOD-LINKED GANGSTER KILLED IN JOINT POLICE ENCOUNTER
paragraphs: Naseem Durrani, who was linked to underworld figure Dawood Ibrahim, was killed in a joint operation by Delhi Police and Noida STF in Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh.
Investigators were examining his suspected role in the November 16 shooting death of a man outside Delhi Law Minister Kapil Mishra's camp office, The Indian Express reported.

stories.source: NDTV / Confederation of All India Traders
stories.headline: 52 LAKH WEDDINGS COULD GENERATE ₹7.5 LAKH CRORE IN BUSINESS
paragraphs: India is expected to host 52 lakh weddings between November 21 and December 15, generating an estimated ₹7.5 lakh crore in business, according to the traders' body CAIT.
The forecast spans retail, hospitality, transport, food and jewellery, with Delhi-NCR expected to account for around five lakh weddings and ₹2.5 lakh crore.

stories.headline: JAISWAL AND RAHUL SET A NEW-CENTURY OPENING RECORD IN NEW ZEALAND
paragraphs: Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul put on 130 runs in the first Test at Wellington, India's first century opening partnership on New Zealand soil this century.
Jaiswal made 85 from 89 balls as India reached 159 for one at stumps on day two, The News Mill reported with ANI inputs.

stories.headline: INDIA STARTS TITLE DEFENCE WITH 4–1 WIN OVER MALAYSIA
paragraphs: India came from behind to beat Malaysia 4–1 in its opening match of the Women's Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal.
Mumtaz Khan scored on her return and debutant Puja Sahoo also found the net as India began its title defence with a win.

stories.headline: BOMBAY HIGH COURT WEIGHS COMPLETE FIRECRACKER BAN OVER POOR AIR
paragraphs: The Bombay High Court expressed concern over poor air quality after Diwali and is considering a complete ban on firecrackers in Mumbai.
The court criticised the lack of compliance with existing restrictions as it weighed stronger measures, The Indian Express reported.
